attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack essay. The quoted tweets in the context are separate material and are not used as the claim.

semantics.note: The context ties the prediction to the US government partly owning the company. 'Are not going to' is a firm forecast for OpenAI. The Google part is hedged with 'maybe', so it is not scored. Calling the Google 'maybe' an antecedent is wrong: it is a hedge, not a condition. The proposition itself is faithful.

contract.note: Requiring an actual completed ownership stake and broad distrust in both regions is a fair, ordinary reading. It correctly sets aside the hedged Google clause and adds no deadline. Nothing turns on an interpretation the speaker did not supply, because the condition is not met.

evidence.note: TIME interview (event Sep 28, published Oct 1, 2026). Trump says only that he might take stakes in OpenAI and Anthropic. That is a possibility, not completed ownership.

Tom's Hardware, Jul 2, 2026, summarising FT reporting. Describes early-stage talks about a 5% stake, possibly needing Congress. This does not establish ownership, and it says nothing about trust in Europe or Asia.

reviews.rationale: The antecedent, actual US government ownership of OpenAI or Google, is not established by the cutoff. The evidence shows only talks and Trump saying he 'might'. There is also no evidence on trust in Europe or Asia. No deadline was stated, and no conclusive event meets the early-resolution rule, so the conditional forecast cannot be scored yet. The hedged Google clause is not scored in any case.
